claim: Amyloid aggregation of phosphorylated Tau (pTau) into neurofibrillary tangles is closely associated with Alzheimer's disease (AD).
source: Amyloid aggregation of phosphorylated Tau (pTau) into neurofibrillary tangles is closely associated with Alzheimer's disease (AD).
evidence: This is a well-established fact in AD research, representing established scientific consensus.

claim: Several molecular chaperones have been reported to bind Tau and impede its pathological aggregation.
source: Several molecular chaperones have been reported to bind Tau and impede its pathological aggregation.
evidence: This statement references prior research findings in the field.

claim: Elevated levels of Hsp27 have been found in the brains of patients with AD.
source: Recent findings of elevated levels of Hsp27 in the brains of patients with AD suggested its important role in pTau pathology.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research and confirmed by data in this manuscript.

claim: Hsp27 partially co-localizes with pTau tangles in the brains of patients with AD.
source: Here, we show that Hsp27 partially co-localizes with pTau tangles in the brains of patients with AD.
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunofluorescence staining data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Phosphorylation of Tau by microtubule affinity regulating kinase 2 (MARK2) dramatically enhances the binding affinity of Hsp27 to Tau.
source: Notably, phosphorylation of Tau by microtubule affinity regulating kinase 2 (MARK2), dramatically enhances the binding affinity of Hsp27 to Tau.
evidence: This is supported by BLI binding affinity measurements presented in the manuscript.

claim: Hsp27 efficiently prevents pTau fibrillation in vitro.
source: Moreover, Hsp27 efficiently prevents pTau fibrillation in vitro and mitigates neuropathology of pTau aggregation in a Drosophila tauopathy model.
evidence: This is demonstrated by ThT fluorescence assays and TEM microscopy data.

claim: Hsp27 mitigates neuropathology of pTau aggregation in a Drosophila tauopathy model.
source: Moreover, Hsp27 efficiently prevents pTau fibrillation in vitro and mitigates neuropathology of pTau aggregation in a Drosophila tauopathy model.
evidence: This is supported by in vivo experiments in Drosophila showing reduced pTau pathology.

claim: Hsp27 employs its N-terminal domain to directly interact with multiple phosphorylation sites of pTau for specific binding.
source: Further mechanistic study reveals that Hsp27 employs its N-terminal domain to directly interact with multiple phosphorylation sites of pTau for specific binding.
evidence: This is demonstrated by NMR titration experiments, BLI assays with domain truncations, and cross-linking mass spectrometry.

claim: Pathological aggregation and propagation of microtubule-associated protein Tau is closely associated with Alzheimer's disease (AD), frontotemporal dementia (FTD), and other tauopathies.
source: Pathological aggregation and propagation of microtubule-associated protein Tau is closely associated with Alzheimer's disease (AD), frontotemporal dementia (FTD), and other tauopathies (Avila, 2006; Hanger et al., 2009; Hanger et al., 1998; Hanger et al., 1991; Spillantini and Goedert, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to established literature.

claim: Tau is hyper-phosphorylated and forms amyloid fibrils in neurofibrillary tangles (NFT) in patients' brains which is the pathological hallmark of AD.
source: Tau is hyper-phosphorylated and forms amyloid fibrils in neurofibrillary tangles (NFT) in patients' brains which is the pathological hallmark of AD.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about AD pathology.

claim: Tau is abundant in the axons of neurons where it stabilizes microtubules.
source: Tau is abundant in the axons of neurons where it stabilizes microtubules (MT; Drechsel et al., 1992; Drubin and Kirschner, 1986).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Abnormal phosphorylation of Tau in the regions surrounding the microtubule-binding domain by kinases such as MARK and GSK3 leads to dissociation of Tau from MT and subsequent pathological aggregation.
source: Under diseased conditions, abnormal phosphorylation of Tau in the regions surrounding the microtubule-binding domain by kinases such as microtubule affinity regulating kinase (MARK) and glycogen synthase kinase 3 (GSK3) leads to dissociation of Tau from MT and subsequent pathological aggregation (Ando et al., 2016; Biernat et al., 1993; Drewes, 2004; Drewes et al., 1997; Hanger et al., 2009; Martin et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: Amyloid fibrils formed by phosphorylated Tau (pTau) are more potent in mediating the propagation and spread of Tau pathology than those formed by unphosphorylated Tau.
source: Moreover, the amyloid fibrils formed by phosphorylated Tau (pTau) have been found to be more potent in mediating the propagation and spread of Tau pathology than those formed by unphosphorylated Tau (Dujardin et al., 2020; Hu et al., 2016; Rosenqvist et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Pathological pTau fibrils have been extracted from AD brains, and Hsp27 has been found to co-precipitate with them.
source: Pathological pTau fibrils have been extracted from AD brains, and Hsp27 has been found to co-precipitate with them (Shimura et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Hsp27 is a member of the small heat shock protein (sHsp) family which participates in the cellular chaperone network to maintain protein homeostasis by preventing protein abnormal aggregation.
source: Hsp27 is a member of the small heat shock protein (sHsp) family which participates in the cellular chaperone network to maintain protein homeostasis by preventing protein abnormal aggregation (Haslbeck et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research and represents established knowledge.

claim: Hsp27 is ubiquitously expressed and plays a protective role in a variety of cellular processes.
source: It is ubiquitously expressed and plays a protective role in a variety of cellular processes (Jakob et al., 1993).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The expression level of Hsp27 is significantly elevated in affected brain tissues of patients with AD.
source: For instance, the expression level of Hsp27 is significantly elevated in affected brain tissues of patients with AD (Björkdahl et al., 2008; Renkawek et al., 1994), as well as patients with other tauopathies including progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) and corticobasal degeneration (CBD) (Schwarz et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The expression level of Hsp27 is significantly elevated in patients with other tauopathies including progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) and corticobasal degeneration (CBD).
source: For instance, the expression level of Hsp27 is significantly elevated in affected brain tissues of patients with AD (Björkdahl et al., 2008; Renkawek et al., 1994), as well as patients with other tauopathies including progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) and corticobasal degeneration (CBD) (Schwarz et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Hsp27 can effectively inhibit the amyloid aggregation of unphosphorylated Tau in vitro.
source: Moreover, Hsp27 can effectively inhibit the amyloid aggregation of unphosphorylated Tau in vitro (Baughman et al., 2018; Baughman et al., 2020; Freilich et al., 2018), prevent cellular toxicity of Tau in SH-SY5Y cells (Choi et al., 2015), and rescue tauopathies in Tau transgenic mice (Abisambra et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Hsp27 can prevent cellular toxicity of Tau in SH-SY5Y cells.
source: Moreover, Hsp27 can effectively inhibit the amyloid aggregation of unphosphorylated Tau in vitro (Baughman et al., 2018; Baughman et al., 2020; Freilich et al., 2018), prevent cellular toxicity of Tau in SH-SY5Y cells (Choi et al., 2015), and rescue tauopathies in Tau transgenic mice (Abisambra et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Hsp27 can rescue tauopathies in Tau transgenic mice.
source: Moreover, Hsp27 can effectively inhibit the amyloid aggregation of unphosphorylated Tau in vitro (Baughman et al., 2018; Baughman et al., 2020; Freilich et al., 2018), prevent cellular toxicity of Tau in SH-SY5Y cells (Choi et al., 2015), and rescue tauopathies in Tau transgenic mice (Abisambra et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: pTau was detected in two AD cases but absent in two healthy controls.
source: Immunofluorescence staining using antibodies anti-pTauSer262 and anti-Hsp27 detected the presence of pTau in two AD cases, but absent in two healthy controls (Figure 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Hsp27 was detected at a high level in AD brain slices, but at a much lower or undetectable level in healthy control brain slices.
source: Notably, Hsp27 was detected at a high level in AD brain slices, but at a much lower or undetectable level in healthy control brain slices (Figure 1), consistent with previous findings of elevated Hsp27 levels in AD brains (Björkdahl et al., 2008; Renkawek et al., 1994).
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunofluorescence data in Figure 1 and is consistent with cited previous research.

claim: Hsp27 co-localizes with pTau aggregates in both AD cases.
source: More importantly, Hsp27 was found to co-localize with the pTau aggregates in both AD cases (Figure 1), suggesting the pathological relevance between Hsp27 and pTau pathology in AD.
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Not all pTau aggregates contain Hsp27 and vice versa, especially in case 1, which may reflect the heterogeneity of the protein aggregates.
source: Note that not all pTau aggregates contain Hsp27 and vice versa, especially in case 1, which may reflect the heterogeneity of the protein aggregates.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the immunofluorescence data and represents speculation about the heterogeneity.

claim: Expression of human TauR406W in the Drosophila nervous system leads to age-dependent neurodegeneration recapitulating some of the salient features of tauopathy in FTDP-17.
source: Our previous work has demonstrated that the expression of human TauR406W in the Drosophila nervous system leads to age-dependent neurodegeneration recapitulating some of the salient features of tauopathy in FTDP-17 (Ali et al., 2012; Ma et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work by the authors.

claim: Hsp27 overexpression significantly reduced hyper-phosphorylated Tau levels at 2 and 10 days after eclosion (DAE).
source: Hsp27 overexpression significantly reduced hyper-phosphorylated Tau levels 2 and 10 days after eclosion (DAE) (Figure 2A and B, Figure 2—source data 1; Figure 2—source data 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot analysis shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: Brains with neuronal expression of TauR406W exhibited an accumulation of filamentous pTau and a reduction of brain neuropil size indicative of neurodegeneration.
source: Consistent with previous findings, brains with neuronal expression of TauR406W exhibited an accumulation of filamentous pTau and a reduction of brain neuropil size indicative of neurodegeneration (Figure 2C–F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunofluorescence staining and quantification shown in Figure 2C-F.

claim: Neuronal expression of TauR406W led to a significant upregulation of endogenous Hsp27, which was highly enriched in the synaptic areas.
source: Interestingly, we found that neuronal expression of TauR406W led to a significant upregulation of endogenous Hsp27, which was highly enriched in the synaptic areas (Figure 2C and D), suggesting that Hsp27 might be a part of the neuronal stress response network that is upregulated upon proteotoxic stress.
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunofluorescence data in Figure 2C and D.

claim: Hsp27 might be a part of the neuronal stress response network that is upregulated upon proteotoxic stress.
source: Interestingly, we found that neuronal expression of TauR406W led to a significant upregulation of endogenous Hsp27, which was highly enriched in the synaptic areas (Figure 2C and D), suggesting that Hsp27 might be a part of the neuronal stress response network that is upregulated upon proteotoxic stress.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the observed upregulation of Hsp27.

claim: Overexpression of Hsp27 restored the size of brain neuropil and suppressed the accumulation of filamentous pTau.
source: Importantly, overexpression of Hsp27 restored the size of brain neuropil and suppressed the accumulation of filamentous pTau (Figure 2C–F), suggesting that Hsp27 protects against mutant TauR406W induced neurodegeneration.
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunofluorescence data and quantification in Figure 2C-F.

claim: Hsp27 protects against mutant TauR406W induced neurodegeneration.
source: Importantly, overexpression of Hsp27 restored the size of brain neuropil and suppressed the accumulation of filamentous pTau (Figure 2C–F), suggesting that Hsp27 protects against mutant TauR406W induced neurodegeneration.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed restoration of neuropil size and suppression of pTau accumulation.

claim: Synaptic loss is a hallmark of human tauopathy.
source: Synaptic loss is a hallmark of human tauopathy (McGowan et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research and represents established knowledge.

claim: TauR406W expression resulted in synaptic aggregation of hyper-phosphorylated Tau as well as a significant reduction of Bruchpilot (Brp) at lamina cartridge, suggesting a severe loss of the active zone structures in the presynaptic terminals.
source: We have previously shown that TauR406W expression resulted in synaptic aggregation of hyper-phosphorylated Tau as well as a significant reduction of Bruchpilot (Brp), an active zone associated-cytoskeletal matrix protein, at lamina cartridge, suggesting a severe loss of the active zone structures in the presynaptic terminals (Ma et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Overexpression of Hsp27 led to a remarkable reduction of synaptic pTau and enhanced BRP localization, indicating a restoration of synaptic integrity.
source: As shown in Figure 2G–I, we expressed TauR406W with either GFP (control) or Hsp27 in the photoreceptors using GMR-GAL4 and found that overexpression of Hsp27 led to a remarkable reduction of synaptic pTau and enhanced BRP localization, indicating a restoration of synaptic integrity.
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunofluorescence data and quantification in Figure 2G-I.

claim: Hsp27 protects against synaptic dysfunction in a Drosophila tauopathy model by reducing pTau aggregation and ameliorating pTau-induced synaptic degeneration.
source: Taken together, we showed that Hsp27 protects against synaptic dysfunction in a Drosophila tauopathy model by reducing pTau aggregation and ameliorating pTau-induced synaptic degeneration.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the Drosophila experimental data presented.

claim: Eight MARK2 phosphorylation sites including pS262, pS293, pS305, pS324, pS352, pS356, pS413, and pS416 were identified on the HSQC spectrum of pTau40.
source: Consistent with previous report (Schwalbe et al., 2013), eight MARK2 phosphorylation sites including pS262, pS293, pS305, pS324, pS352, pS356, pS413, and pS416 were identified on the HSQC spectrum of pTau40 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by NMR spectroscopy data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and is consistent with cited previous research.

claim: Four phosphorylation sites including pS262, pS324, pS352, and pS356 were identified on the HSQC spectrum of pK19.
source: Four phosphorylation sites including pS262, pS324, pS352, and pS356 were identified on the HSQC spectrum of pK19 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by NMR spectroscopy data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Most of the MARK2 phosphorylation sites are within the fibril forming core region of Tau.
source: Most of these phosphorylation sites are within the fibril forming core region of Tau, and two of them including pS262 and pS356 have been widely reported to be essential for the detachment of pTau from MT and cause increased toxicity in animal models (Hanger et al., 1998; Hanger et al., 2009; Ali et al., 2012).
evidence: This is based on structural knowledge of Tau and is supported by citations.

claim: pS262 and pS356 have been widely reported to be essential for the detachment of pTau from MT and cause increased toxicity in animal models.
source: Most of these phosphorylation sites are within the fibril forming core region of Tau, and two of them including pS262 and pS356 have been widely reported to be essential for the detachment of pTau from MT and cause increased toxicity in animal models (Hanger et al., 1998; Hanger et al., 2009; Ali et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The KD value of Hsp27/pTau40 is approximately 1.58 µM.
source: Notably, the KD value of Hsp27/pTau40 is ~1.58 µM (Figure 3B; Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This is determined by BLI assay data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The KD value for Hsp27/pK19 is approximately 1.98 µM.
source: The KD value for Hsp27/pK19 is ~1.98 µM (Figure 3C; Figure 3—source data 1) which is similar to that of Hsp27/pTau40.
evidence: This is determined by BLI assay data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Both the association (kon) and dissociation (koff) rates of Hsp27 to pK19 are at the same order of magnitude of Hsp27 to pTau40.
source: In addition, both the association (kon) and dissociation (koff) rates of Hsp27 to pK19 are at the same order of magnitude of Hsp27 to pTau40.
evidence: This is based on the BLI kinetic data presented in Figures 3B and 3C.

claim: pK19 serves as the key region for binding of Hsp27 to pTau40.
source: These results suggest that pK19 serves as the key region for binding of Hsp27 to pTau40.
evidence: This is an inference based on the similar binding affinities of Hsp27 to pK19 and pTau40.

claim: The binding of both Hsp27/Tau40 and Hsp27/K19 were much weaker which cannot be detectable under the experimental condition.
source: In sharp comparison, the binding of both Hsp27/Tau40 and Hsp27/K19 were much weaker which cannot be detectable under our experimental condition (Figure 3B and C; Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by BLI assay data shown in Figures 3B and 3C.

claim: Hyper-phosphorylation significantly enhances the binding of Hsp27 to both pTau40 and pK19.
source: These results demonstrate that hyper-phosphorylation significantly enhances the binding of Hsp27 to both pTau40 and pK19.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the comparison of binding affinities between phosphorylated and unphosphorylated Tau.

claim: Hsp27 effectively inhibited the amyloid aggregation of both pTau40 and pK19 in a dose-dependent manner.
source: The results showed that Hsp27 effectively inhibited the amyloid aggregation of both pTau40 and pK19 in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 3D and E; Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by ThT fluorescence assay and TEM data shown in Figures 3D and 3E.

claim: Hsp27 can specifically bind to hyper-phosphorylated Tau including pTau40 and pK19, and efficiently prevent their amyloid aggregation.
source: Together, our data show that Hsp27 can specifically bind to hyper-phosphorylated Tau including pTau40 and pK19, and efficiently prevent their amyloid aggregation.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the BLI and ThT/TEM data presented.

claim: All eight phosphorylated Ser (pSer) residues of pTau40 showed obvious chemical shift changes (CSDs) upon titration of Hsp27.
source: Strikingly, the 2D 1H-15N HSQC spectra showed obvious chemical shift changes (CSDs) of all the eight phosphorylated Ser (pSer) residues of pTau40 and four pSer residues of pK19 upon titration of Hsp27 (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by NMR titration data shown in Figures 4A and 4B.

claim: All four pSer residues of pK19 showed obvious chemical shift changes (CSDs) upon titration of Hsp27.
source: Strikingly, the 2D 1H-15N HSQC spectra showed obvious chemical shift changes (CSDs) of all the eight phosphorylated Ser (pSer) residues of pTau40 and four pSer residues of pK19 upon titration of Hsp27 (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by NMR titration data shown in Figures 4A and 4B.

claim: The regions containing the four pSer residues of pK19 harbor prominent CSDs.
source: As shown in Figure 3C, the regions containing the four pSer residues of pK19 harbor prominent CSDs.
evidence: This is demonstrated by NMR titration data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The two pSer residues in R4 showed the largest CSDs above 0.06 ppm.
source: Among them, the two pSer residues in R4 showed the largest CSDs above 0.06 ppm (Figure 4C; Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by NMR titration data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Titration of Hsp27 to pK19 induced dramatically intensity drops of most residues of pK19.
source: In addition, titration of Hsp27 to pK19 induced dramatically intensity drops of most residues of pK19 (Figure 4C; Figure 4—source data 1), implying the direct binding of Hsp27 to pK19 which increases the molecular weight upon pK19-Hsp27 complex formation, and thus increases line width of the cross peaks.
evidence: This is demonstrated by NMR titration data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The intensity drops imply the direct binding of Hsp27 to pK19 which increases the molecular weight upon pK19-Hsp27 complex formation, and thus increases line width of the cross peaks.
source: In addition, titration of Hsp27 to pK19 induced dramatically intensity drops of most residues of pK19 (Figure 4C; Figure 4—source data 1), implying the direct binding of Hsp27 to pK19 which increases the molecular weight upon pK19-Hsp27 complex formation, and thus increases line width of the cross peaks.
evidence: This is an inference based on NMR principles and the observed intensity changes.

claim: Addition of Hsp27 to unphosphorylated Tau including Tau40 and K19 only results in slightly CSD and intensity perturbations.
source: By contrast, addition of the same amount of Hsp27 to unphosphorylated Tau including Tau40 and K19 only results in slightly CSD and intensity perturbations (Figure 4—figure supplement 1; Figure 4—figure supplement 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by NMR titration data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Phosphorylation of Tau promotes the interaction between Hsp27 and pTau by forming the specific interaction between Hsp27 and the phosphorylated residues of Tau.
source: Together, our data suggest that phosphorylation of Tau promotes the interaction between Hsp27 and pTau by forming the specific interaction between Hsp27 and the phosphorylated residues of Tau.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the NMR titration data comparing phosphorylated and unphosphorylated Tau.

claim: The isolated NTD binds to pK19 with a KD value of approximately 0.57 µM which is similar to the binding affinity of the full-length Hsp27 to pK19.
source: Notably, the isolated NTD binds to pK19 with a KD value of ~0.57 µM which is similar to the binding affinity of the full-length Hsp27 to pK19 (Figure 5B; Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: This is determined by BLI assay data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: ΔCTD which contains both NTD and ACD display a similar binding affinity to pK19 (0.67±0.01 µM).
source: ΔCTD which contains both NTD and ACD display a similar binding affinity to pK19 (0.67±0.01 µM; Figure 5B; Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: This is determined by BLI assay data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Both ACD and ΔNTD which do not contain NTD show no detectable binding to pK19 at the same condition.
source: In contrast, both ACD and ΔNTD which do not contain NTD show no detectable binding to pK19 at the same condition (Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1; Figure 5—figure supplement 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by BLI assay data shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Hsp27 NTD plays an essential role in mediating the binding of Hsp27 to pK19.
source: Together, these data suggest that Hsp27 NTD plays an essential role in mediating the binding of Hsp27 to pK19.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the BLI data with domain truncations.

claim: Two pairs of cross-linked segments between Hsp27 and pK19 were identified including E3Hsp27-K331pK19 and D30Hsp27-K311pK19.
source: We identified two pairs of cross-linked segments between Hsp27 and pK19 with a confidence score of <10–6 by mass spectrometry, including E3Hsp27-K331pK19 and D30Hsp27-K311pK19 (Figure 5D and E and Table 2).
evidence: This is determined by cross-linking mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 5D and E and Table 2.

claim: Both cross-linked segments are formed by residues located at R3 of pK19 and NTD of Hsp27.
source: Notably, both cross-linked segments are formed by residues located at R3 of pK19 and NTD of Hsp27 (Figure 5D), which is consistent with our NMR titration that residues at R3 show slightly stronger intensity drop upon addition of Hsp27, and the domain truncation mapping results.
evidence: This is demonstrated by cross-linking mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: NTD is essential to mediate pK19 binding.
source: Together, our data demonstrate that NTD is essential to mediate pK19 binding.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the BLI, NMR, and cross-linking mass spectrometry data.

claim: Titration of both NTD and ΔCTD induce significant CSDs mainly located on the four pSer sites of pK19.
source: Titration of both NTD and ΔCTD induce significant CSDs mainly located on the four pSer sites of pK19 (Figure 6A and B; Figure 6—source data 1), which recapitulates that titrated by full-length Hsp27.
evidence: This is demonstrated by NMR titration data shown in Figures 6A and 6B.

claim: Titration of ACD or ΔNTD caused much smaller CSDs on the four pSer sites of pK19.
source: In contrast, titration of ACD or ΔNTD caused much smaller CSDs on the four pSer sites of pK19.
evidence: This is demonstrated by NMR titration data shown in Figures 6A and 6B.

claim: Addition of NTD and ΔCTD induces overall intensity drops of pK19 signals (~I/I0<0.8), while titration of ACD and ΔNTD only cause slightly intensity drops.
source: Moreover, addition of NTD and ΔCTD induces overall intensity drops of pK19 signals (~I/I0<0.8), while titration of ACD and ΔNTD only cause slightly intensity drops.
evidence: This is demonstrated by NMR titration data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Hsp27 mainly uses its NTD to directly interact with the pSer residues of pK19 for pTau binding.
source: These results demonstrate that Hsp27 mainly uses its NTD to directly interact with the pSer residues of pK19 for pTau binding, which is consistent with the BLI results.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the NMR titration data with domain truncations.

claim: Titration of ACD causes relative small but detectable CSDs (>0.01 ppm) and intensity drops (I/I0<0.7) of the highly amyloidogenic region - 306VQIVYK311 of pK19, especially residues V309, Y310, and K311.
source: Notably, we found that despite that titration of ACD does not induce CSDs of the pSer sites, it causes relative small but detectable CSDs (>0.01 ppm) and intensity drops (I/I0<0.7) of the highly amyloidogenic region - 306VQIVYK311 of pK19, especially residues V309, Y310, and K311 (Figure 6A and B; Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by NMR titration data shown in Figures 6A and 6B.

claim: ACD is capable of directly binding to pK19 via its VQIVYK region.
source: This demonstrates that ACD is capable of directly binding to pK19 via its VQIVYK region.
evidence: This is an inference based on the NMR titration data showing CSDs and intensity drops in the VQIVYK region.

claim: Different domains of Hsp27 display distinct binding preferences to different regions of pK19.
source: Together, our results demonstrate that different domains of Hsp27 display distinct binding preferences to different regions of pK19.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the NMR titration data with domain truncations.

claim: NTD exhibits a high binding affinity to the multiple pSer sites of pK19, while ACD weakly binds the amyloidogenic VQIVYK segment of pK19.
source: NTD exhibits a high binding affinity to the multiple pSer sites of pK19, while ACD weakly binds the amyloidogenic VQIVYK segment of pK19.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the NMR and BLI data with domain truncations.

claim: NTD-containing Hsp27 variants including full-length Hsp27, ΔCTD, and NTD exhibits potent inhibitory activity in preventing both pTau40 and pK19 fibrillation.
source: As shown in Figure 7A and B (Figure 7—source data 1), NTD-containing Hsp27 variants including full-length Hsp27, ΔCTD, and NTD exhibits potent inhibitory activity in preventing both pTau40 and pK19 fibrillation.
evidence: This is demonstrated by ThT fluorescence assay and TEM data shown in Figures 7A and 7B.

claim: Strong binding of NTD to the phosphorylated sites of pTau is important in preventing pTau fibrillation.
source: This suggests that strong binding of NTD to the phosphorylated sites of pTau is important in preventing pTau fibrillation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the correlation between NTD binding and inhibitory activity.

claim: ACD and ΔNTD display weakened but not negligible inhibitory activity of pTau, especially for pK19.
source: Interestingly, ACD and ΔNTD display weakened but not negligible inhibitory activity of pTau, especially for pK19.
evidence: This is demonstrated by ThT fluorescence assay and TEM data shown in Figures 7A and 7B.

claim: Binding of ACD to the VQIVYK segment of pTau may result in moderate inhibition of pTau fibrillation.
source: This suggests that binding of ACD to the VQIVYK segment of pTau may result in moderate inhibition of pTau fibrillation.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the observed moderate inhibitory activity of ACD.

claim: The NTD is predominately employed to bind pTau to prevent its fibrillation, while ACD also contributes chaperone activity to a less degree by binding to the highly aggregation-prone VQIVYK region of pTau.
source: Together, our data show that the NTD is predominately employed to bind pTau to prevent its fibrillation, while ACD also contributes chaperone activity to a less degree by binding to the highly aggregation-prone VQIVYK region of pTau.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the NMR, BLI, and ThT/TEM data with domain truncations.

claim: Many molecular chaperones including Hsp70, DnaJA2, Hsp90, Hsp27, and NMNAT can directly interact with Tau and are involved in different steps of Tau biogenesis, aggregation, and clearance.
source: Accumulating evidence showed that many molecular chaperones including Hsp70, DnaJA2, Hsp90, Hsp27, and NMNAT can directly interact with Tau and are involved in different steps of Tau biogenesis, aggregation, and clearance (Baughman et al., 2018; Freilich et al., 2018; Ma et al., 2020; Mok et al., 2018; Petrucelli et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Hsp27 was identified to co-precipitate with AD brain-derived pTau aggregates.
source: Since Hsp27 was identified to co-precipitate with AD brain-derived pTau aggregates and is elevated in AD brains (Björkdahl et al., 2008; Renkawek et al., 1994; Shimura et al., 2004), Hsp27 may play an important role in interacting with pTau in AD.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Hsp27 may play an important role in interacting with pTau in AD.
source: Since Hsp27 was identified to co-precipitate with AD brain-derived pTau aggregates and is elevated in AD brains (Björkdahl et al., 2008; Renkawek et al., 1994; Shimura et al., 2004), Hsp27 may play an important role in interacting with pTau in AD.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the co-precipitation and elevation of Hsp27 in AD.

claim: MARK2-mediated phosphorylation of Tau dramatically increases the binding of pTau to Hsp27.
source: Indeed, we showed elevated Hsp27 levels and partial co-localization of Hsp27 with pTau aggregates in AD brains. More importantly, we found that MARK2-mediated phosphorylation of Tau dramatically increases the binding of pTau to Hsp27, strengthening the notion that Hsp27 binds specifically to disease-related pTau.
evidence: This is demonstrated by BLI binding affinity measurements presented in the manuscript.

claim: Hsp27 binds specifically to disease-related pTau.
source: Indeed, we showed elevated Hsp27 levels and partial co-localization of Hsp27 with pTau aggregates in AD brains. More importantly, we found that MARK2-mediated phosphorylation of Tau dramatically increases the binding of pTau to Hsp27, strengthening the notion that Hsp27 binds specifically to disease-related pTau.
evidence: This is an inference based on the enhanced binding to MARK2-phosphorylated Tau.

claim: This specific binding enables Hsp27 to be a potent chaperone in inhibiting amyloid aggregation of MARK2-mediated phosphorylated Tau in vitro.
source: This specific binding enables Hsp27 to be a potent chaperone in inhibiting amyloid aggregation of MARK2-mediated phosphorylated Tau in vitro.
evidence: This is an inference based on the binding and aggregation inhibition data.

claim: Over 58 different phosphorylation sites including MARK2-phosphorylation sites were identified on Tau40 in AD brains.
source: Over 58 different phosphorylation sites including MARK2-phosphorylation sites were identified on Tau40 in AD brains (Hanger et al., 1998; Hanger et al., 2007; Hasegawa et al., 1992; Morishima-Kawashima et al., 1995; Wesseling et al., 2020; Xia et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Phosphorylation at different sites is believed to be involved in different stages of pTau pathology in AD.
source: Phosphorylation at different sites is believed to be involved in different stages of pTau pathology in AD (Hanger et al., 2009; Wesseling et al., 2020; Xia et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Hsp27 exhibits potent inhibitory activity on S356E Tau but not the other Tau phosphomimetics.
source: Strikingly, Hsp27 exhibits potent inhibitory activity on S356E Tau but not the other Tau phosphomimetics (Mok et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The potent inhibitory activity of Hsp27 on S356E Tau suggests the binding specificity of Hsp27 on different phosphorylation sites of Tau.
source: Strikingly, Hsp27 exhibits potent inhibitory activity on S356E Tau but not the other Tau phosphomimetics (Mok et al., 2018). This suggests the binding specificity of Hsp27 on different phosphorylation sites of Tau.
evidence: This is an inference based on the differential inhibitory activity on different phosphomimetics.

claim: Other molecular chaperones including Hsp90 and NMNAT were also found to mediate pTau cellular clearance and prevent pTau aggregation both in vitro and in cells.
source: Moreover, other molecular chaperones including Hsp90 and NMNAT were also found to mediate pTau cellular clearance and prevent pTau aggregation both in vitro and in cells (Dickey et al., 2007; Ma et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Hsp27 uses its NTD to strongly bind to the multiple phosphorylation sites of pTau.
source: We showed in this study that Hsp27 uses its NTD to strongly bind to the multiple phosphorylation sites of pTau.
evidence: This is demonstrated by NMR, BLI, and cross-linking mass spectrometry data.

claim: ACD of Hsp27 transiently and weakly interacts with the highly amyloidogenic region - 306VQIVYK311 of pTau.
source: Meanwhile, ACD of Hsp27 transiently and weakly interacts with the highly amyloidogenic region - 306VQIVYK311 of pTau.
evidence: This is demonstrated by NMR titration data.

claim: Different domains of Hsp27 are responsible for binding to distinct regions of pTau.
source: Therefore, different domains of Hsp27 are responsible for binding to distinct regions of pTau.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the NMR and BLI data with domain truncations.

claim: For unphosphorylated Tau, ACD exhibits the strongest binding ability by predominantly binding the 306VQIVYK311 region of Tau via its β4 and β8 region.
source: Notably, previous studies showed that, as for the unphosphorylated Tau, ACD exhibits the strongest binding ability by predominantly binding the 306VQIVYK311 region of Tau via its β4 and β8 region (Baughman et al., 2018; Baughman et al., 2020; Freilich et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: NTD displays much weaker binding to unmodified Tau.
source: While NTD displays much weaker binding to unmodified Tau (Baughman et al., 2020; Freilich et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Phosphorylation of Tau shifts the paradigm of Hsp27 binding pattern of Tau, which results in significantly enhanced overall binding of Hsp27 to pTau.
source: Therefore, phosphorylation of Tau shifts the paradigm of Hsp27 binding pattern of Tau, which results in significantly enhanced overall binding of Hsp27 to pTau.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the comparison of binding patterns between phosphorylated and unphosphorylated Tau.

claim: The phosphorylation pattern of pTau is dynamically changed upon the progression of AD.
source: As the phosphorylation pattern of pTau is dynamically changed upon the progression of AD (Hanger et al., 2009; Wesseling et al., 2020; Xia et al., 2021), how phosphorylation at different sites influences the interplay between pTau and its binding patterns including Hsp27 and different molecular chaperones will be interesting to investigate.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: NTD of Hsp27 is essential for binding to the phosphorylation sites of pTau.
source: This study demonstrates that NTD of Hsp27 is essential for binding to the phosphorylation sites of pTau.
evidence: This is demonstrated by NMR, BLI, and cross-linking mass spectrometry data.

claim: Hsp27 was found to be phosphorylated at multiple sites on NTD under stress conditions, which leads to dissociation of Hsp27 from high-molecular-weight oligomers to smaller ones with higher chaperone activities.
source: Notably, Hsp27 was found to be phosphorylated at multiple sites on NTD under stress conditions, which leads to dissociation of Hsp27 from high-molecular-weight oligomers to smaller ones with higher chaperone activities (Alderson et al., 2019; Jovcevski et al., 2017; Jovcevski et al., 2015; Lambert et al., 1999; Rogalla et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: NTD phosphorylation provides an additional layer for regulating Hsp27 activity in controlling the phase separation and amyloid fibrillation of ALS-associated FUS.
source: Our previous work showed that NTD phosphorylation provides an additional layer for regulating Hsp27 activity in controlling the phase separation and amyloid fibrillation of ALS-associated FUS (Liu et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: The study demonstrates the important role of Hsp27 in chaperoning pathological pTau from abnormal aggregation.
source: Nevertheless, our study demonstrates the important role of Hsp27 in chaperoning pathological pTau from abnormal aggregation, and implies that activating Hsp27 or elevating its level might be a potential strategy for AD treatment.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on all the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Activating Hsp27 or elevating its level might be a potential strategy for AD treatment.
source: Nevertheless, our study demonstrates the important role of Hsp27 in chaperoning pathological pTau from abnormal aggregation, and implies that activating Hsp27 or elevating its level might be a potential strategy for AD treatment.
evidence: This is a speculative implication based on the findings of the study.
